'''Veluws''' is a dialect or an umbrella term for dialects which are spoken in [[Veluwe]], in the northwest of [[Gelderland]], in central [[Netherlands]].

==Dialects==
[[File:Frans Nieuwenhuis 2.jpg|thumb|left|[[Frans Nieuwenhuis]] (born 1936) sings in the Veluws dialect.]]
Veluws is usually divided into two [[dialect|main dialects]], [[West-Veluws]] and [[Oost-Veluws dialect|Oost-Veluws]] (East Veluws), these two dialects are reasonably similar but differ in [[grammar]]. For example: in Oost-Veluws it is said {{Lang|vel|ie warkt/wärkt}} ('you are working') and in West-Veluws {{Lang|vel|jie warken/waarken}} ('you are working').

West-Veluws has more influence from [[Dutch language|Dutch]]. Typically the closer one gets to the border with Oost-Veluws, the more the dialects differ from Standard Dutch. For example, in the central part where West-Veluws is spoken {{Lang|vel|hie staot}} ('he is standing'); in the northwestern part the corresponding phrase sounds {{Lang|vel|hij steet}}, compared to {{Lang|vel|hij/hee stiet}} in Oost-Veluws. The latter has more Low Saxon influence. In [[Hattem]], the northeastern part where Oost-Veluws is spoken, it has more [[Sallands|Sallandic]] influences.{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}

Westveluws is classified as Low Franconian ({{lang|nl|Nederfrankisch}}), more specifically as belonging to ''{{lang|nl|Hollands-Frankisch}}'', while Oostveluws is Low Saxon ({{lang|nl|Saksisch}}).<ref>E. Rijpma & F. G. Schuringa, edited by Jan van Bakel, ''Nederlandse spraakkunst'', 21st ed., 1967, p. 24, § 8 (also [https://www.dbnl.org/tekst/rijp001nede01_01/ online at dbnl.org])</ref>
In another classification, the dialects in the South and West of [[Veluwe]] (together with e.g. [[North Holland]] and [[Utrecht (province)|Utrecht]]) belong to the Central Dutch varieties and are Low Franconian, while the North and East of Veluwe (together with e.g. [[Salland]]) is part of Overijssel and belong to Low Saxon.<ref>Wilbert Jan Heeringa, ''Measuring Dialect Pronunciation Differences using Levenshtein Distance'', doctor's thesis, 2004, p. 229 and 231 ([http://www.wjheeringa.nl/thesis/ online])</ref>
In another terminology, ''Veluws'' is the dialect of the West, South and Center of [[Veluwe]] (Low Franconian) and ''Sallands'' is the dialect in a small part in the North and the East of Veluwe and [[Salland]] (Low Saxon).<ref>A. A. Weijnen, ''Nederlandse dialectkunde'', 1958, p. 461, ''Kaart 36a - De noordoostelijke dialecten'' ([https://www.dbnl.org/tekst/weij005nede01_01/ online])</ref>
